bihar_raw_news.content: Home · Digital governance Traffic near the Kokapet ORR junction, Hyderabad. Photo: Soumendra Kumar Sahoo via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0) The Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) has started work on CURE-ITMS, an AI-powered Intelligent Traffic Management System that will bring 429 traffic signal locations across the Greater Hyderabad, Cyberabad and Malkajgiri municipal corporations onto one common platform. The GHMC Standing Committee has approved ₹2.83 crore for the Detailed Project Report (DPR), which Osmania University has been given four weeks to prepare, The New Indian Express reported on 23 November 2026. The move is Hyderabad’s latest step towards data-led urban mobility, after earlier projects such as the city’s push to reshape its mobility ecosystem . What the Hyderabad AI traffic system will do CURE-ITMS will cover all 429 signalised junctions inside the Core Urban Region Economy (CURE) limits, with plans to extend the network beyond the Outer Ring Road (ORR). According to GHMC officials, the system is designed to: Adjust signals in real time: regulate traffic dynamically based on live conditions, especially during peak hours and heavy rainfall. Clear the way for emergency vehicles: give priority movement to ambulances and fire services along identified routes. Improve road safety: identify accident-prone locations and add AI-based road safety measures, signage and allied infrastructure. End fragmented maintenance: replace the current piecemeal approach to signal upkeep with a single, integrated network. Osmania University to prepare the DPR GHMC has entrusted the Department of Electrical Engineering at University College of Engineering, Osmania University, with the DPR. The report will set out the technology requirements and implementation framework, and the proposed AI technologies will first be tested through pilot projects before a wider rollout. Identification and installation of additional signals is planned for December 2026. The directions came from review meetings chaired by Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy and the Special Chief Secretary for Municipal Administration and Urban Development, which also called for an Integrated Traffic Data Platform. The state government has proposed a dedicated body, Traffic Management and Road Safety (TG-TMARS), to oversee traffic management and road safety. Why it matters for smart city governance The government has already sanctioned ₹77.31 crore to maintain, upgrade and rewire existing signals and to install 50 new traffic signals and 15 pelican crossings. CURE-ITMS goes further by putting every junction on one AI platform, an approach Indian cities are increasingly adopting through integrated command and control centres and AI-powered urban mobility systems . It also follows Telangana’s other AI-led citizen services, such as the learner’s licence test from home . FAQ What is CURE-ITMS in Hyderabad? CURE-ITMS is a proposed AI-powered Intelligent Traffic Management System that will link 429 traffic signal locations in Hyderabad’s Core Urban Region Economy limits on a common platform to manage traffic in real time. Who is preparing the project report? The Department of Electrical Engineering, University College of Engineering, Osmania University, is preparing the DPR within four weeks, funded by ₹2.83 crore approved by the GHMC Standing Committee. bihar_raw_news.content: News Bihar Floats Tender For Solarisation Of Agricultural Feeders Across State The tender requires an Earnest Money Deposit (EMD)/Security Deposit of Rs. 1 lakh/MW. The deadline for submission of bids through the e-tendering portal is December 31, 2026. Chitrika Grover 25 Nov 2026 10:31 IST Follow Us Bihar State Power Generation Company Limited (BSPGCL) has invited bids for setting up grid-connected solar power plants to solarise segregated and mixed agricultural feeders at power sub-stations. The power generated from these plants will be procured by Bihar's distribution companies (DISCOMs), North Bihar Power Distribution Company Limited (NBPDCL) and South Bihar Power Distribution Company Limited (SBPDCL), at various locations across the state. The projects will be developed under the RESCO mode as part of the Feeder Level Solarisation-State Scheme. Advertisment The tender requires an Earnest Money Deposit (EMD)/Security Deposit of Rs. 1 lakh/MW. The deadline for submission of bids through the e-tendering portal is December 31, 2026. Advertisment The AgriPV system must be designed to facilitate agricultural operations, including irrigation and mechanised farming, with a minimum structural clearance of three metres. It must also ensure that agricultural yield is maintained at no less than 80% of the baseline yield under comparable open-field conditions. BSPGCL has established an online land portal through which farmers across Bihar can upload details of land parcels available for the development of solar power projects. The successful bidder (SPD) may access the portal, upon payment of the applicable access fee, to view details of land parcels uploaded by farmers, including their locations and addresses, and identify suitable land for project development. Advertisment Alternatively, the SPD may arrange its own land for the project. However, the arrangement, acquisition or leasing of land, as well as its suitability for project development, will remain the sole responsibility of the bidder. Additionally, the Project Developer for a solar project developed under an Agri-Photovoltaic (AgriPV) configuration must ensure simultaneous, continuous agricultural production and electricity generation on the same land parcel. Scope Of Work The scope of work includes the design, engineering, supply, construction, erection, testing and commissioning of grid-connected, solar-based power plants (SPPs). It also covers the construction of bays and installation of related switchgear at the substations, along with Remote Monitoring Systems (RMS). The selected developers will also be responsible for comprehensive operation and maintenance of the plants for 25 operational years. Advertisment The projects must be developed in accordance with applicable laws, the Grid Code, the terms and conditions of the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA), and prudent utility practices. The solar power generated will be sold to Bihar DISCOMs at the delivery point at each substation across various locations in the state. bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Plans Ropeways at 20 Tourist Destinations 25 Nov 2026 2 min read Why in News? The Bihar Government , led by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary , is planning to develop ropeway facilities at 20 major tourist destinations across the state to promote religious, historical and eco-tourism. Key Points Patna–Sonepur Ropeway: The proposed 7-km ropeway will connect the JP Ganga Path area in Patna to Hariharnath Temple in Sonepur, Saran district , across the Ganga. Implementation Model: The project is proposed to be developed under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model . Project Announcement: Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced the project in October 2026 at the Rising Bihar Investor Summit in Patna. Six Major Tourist Destinations: Brahmayoni Hill (Gaya), Dungeshwari Hill (Bodh Gaya), Pretshila Hill (Gaya), Vanavar Hill (Jehanabad), Rohtasgarh Fort (Rohtas) and Maa Mundeshwari Temple (Kaimur). Financial Allocation: ₹35.91 crore for three ropeway projects—Brahmayoni Hill (₹8.67 crore), Dungeshwari Hill (₹16.76 crore) and Pretshila Hill (₹10.48 crore). Mundeshwari Ropeway: The Central Government has granted final approval for the use of 1.3094 hectares of forest land for the project. Objectives: To improve connectivity to major religious and tourist destinations and promote religious, historical and eco-tourism across Bihar. (AI image) Delhi's road to lower pollution and cleaner air seems to have run into a substantial barrier. Nearly five months after the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy 2026 came into force, subsidies meant to encourage buyers to switch to commercial EVs have attracted very few applicants. With Delhi getting ready to stop registrations of diesel/petrol/CNG commercial vehicles in a few weeks from now, such dismal buyer response has put its ambitious clean air dream at risk. Also read | Cleaner cars won't clear Delhi's toxic air As the capital's EV plan sputters, the stakes are getting higher not just for car sellers but also for the city in general. According to CAQM data, transport is among the biggest contributors to Delhi's pollution, accounting for 23% of winter pollution, with commercial vehicles having a particularly big share in it. Live Events What Delhi EV Policy seeks to achieve The capital's pollution plan seeks to electrify autos and goods carriers through subsidies, scrappage benefits and better charging infra, alongside a (phased) curb on conventional vehicles, the Delhi EV policy document says. The deadline, after which the transition will be forced into law, is almost at hand. But the sops and the infra on offer have not been able to give a big enough push for that transition to speed up. So, Delhi just found itself faced with a critical challenge: how to sweeten the deal for CV operators' to make them switch to EVs before the clock runs out. The policy has identified three-wheelers, commercial cars and N1-category goods vehicles as critical targets because they cover long distances and remain on roads for long periods, contributing disproportionately to Delhi's pollution. So, electrifying these carriers is among the first things on the govt's mind. The policy, which came into effect on July 1, 2026, aims to accelerate EV adoption, expand charging infra, reduce dependence on petrol/diesel/CNG vehicles and develop battery recycling and servicing facilities. Why subsidies are falling short The Delhi govt is offering Rs 50,000 in subsidy for buying an electric auto in the first year, falling to Rs 40,000 and Rs 30,000 in subsequent years. bihar_raw_news.title: 799 Plastic Waste Management Units Found Only on Paper Across 29 Bihar Districts - The 420.in
bihar_raw_news.content: SHARE Follow us on Google News MUZAFFARPUR: A major discrepancy has surfaced between official records and ground reality regarding plastic waste management in Bihar, where officials across 29 districts claimed on paper to have set up 799 unverified units. According to reports submitted to the state headquarters, these 29 districts claimed that a total of 931 plastic waste management units had been established and were operating at the panchayat level. However, when the central government ordered geo-tagging and photographic proof of these facilities to be uploaded on the official portal, valid records were submitted for only 132 units. Taking serious note of the irregularity, the Chief Executive Officer cum Mission Director of the Lohiya Swachh Bihar Abhiyan has sought explanations from the concerned district officials within three days, warning of strict departmental action if satisfactory replies are not received. Discrepancy Emerges After Geo-Tagging Mandate The issue pertains to the establishment of plastic waste management infrastructure across all panchayats in the state under the Swachhata Hi Seva Abhiyan-2026. Implemented through the Lohiya Swachh Bihar Abhiyan, the initiative aimed to set up waste management units at the village level to ensure the proper disposal of collected plastic waste. When headquarters sought progress reports on the construction and operation of these facilities, officials from 29 districts reported that 931 units were fully established and functional. To verify the actual status of the reported infrastructure on the ground, the Union Ministry of Rural Development directed officials to conduct geo-tagging of each facility and upload photographs to the official IMIS portal of the Swachh Bharat Mission. The objective was to confirm that the units shown in government files physically existed and were actively operating. Despite dozens of official letters and repeated warnings from the department, the 29 districts collectively managed to upload photographic evidence for only 132 units, leaving 799 claimed units completely unverified. Consequently, Lohiya Swachh Bihar Abhiyan CEO cum Mission Director Himanshu Sharma issued notices to the district coordinators and district consultants of all 29 districts, demanding to know why proof could not be provided for the remaining units reported in their official submissions. Sharp Mismatch in Muzaffarpur and Madhubani Records A district-wise review of the submitted data revealed wide gaps between paper claims and actual verification, with Muzaffarpur and Madhubani showing some of the starkest mismatches. In Muzaffarpur, officials reported that 125 plastic waste management units had been set up, whereas ground assessments showed that only three units are actively functioning. Muzaffarpur District Coordinator Ranjeet Kumar Sah stated that plastic waste units have either been constructed in all panchayats or tagged with facilities in neighboring panchayats, though the district still failed to upload adequate photographic proof on the portal. The review found the situation in Madhubani equally concerning, where the administration claimed to have established 150 units but could provide portal records and photos for only five. Similarly, Gayaji district reported 120 established units against proof submitted for just five. In Araria, only one unit was photographed against a claim of 107.

The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, is organising the event. Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj Rajiv Ranjan Singh, also known as Lalan Singh, will attend as the Chief Guest. A major highlight of the celebration will be the presentation of the National Gopal Ratna Awards 2026 by Union Minister Lalan Singh. Among the highest national recognitions in the livestock and dairy sector, the awards recognise outstanding contributions to the promotion and conservation of indigenous cattle and buffalo breeds, dairy development and improved livestock productivity. The awards will be presented in three categories: Best Dairy Farmer Rearing Indigenous Cattle/Buffalo Breeds (Non-NER), Best Artificial Insemination Technician (Non-NER), and Best Dairy Cooperative Society (DCS)/Milk Producer Company/Dairy Farmer Producer Organisation (Non-NER). An Effluent Treatment Plant at Mithila Milk Union (MMU), Samastipur, will also be dedicated. The initiatives are expected to strengthen milk procurement and quality testing, improve animal nutrition and promote environmentally sustainable dairy operations. The event will also mark the dedication to the nation of Namaste India’s 2 lakh litres per day (LLPD) milk processing plant at Sikandarpur, Bihta, Patna. The facility has been established with assistance under the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF). In addition, certificates will be distributed for Veterinary Medicine Sales Centres sanctioned under the Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP), with the aim of improving access to veterinary healthcare services. bihar_raw_news.title: Govt to confer Gopal Ratna awards, release livestock climate roadmap on National Milk Day
bihar_raw_news.content: Advertisement Home / Business / Govt to confer Gopal Ratna awards, release livestock climate roadmap on National Milk Day Govt to confer Gopal Ratna awards, release livestock climate roadmap on National Milk Day NEW DELHI, Nov 24 : The government will confer its National Gopal Ratna Awards, launch a climate-resilience roadmap for the livestock and dairy sector and inaugurate several dairy infrastructure projects at National Milk Day celebrations in Patna. Union Minister for... Daily Excelsior 04:20 AM Nov 25, 2026 IST NEW DELHI, Nov 24 : The government will confer its National Gopal Ratna Awards, launch a climate-resilience roadmap for the livestock and dairy sector and inaugurate several dairy infrastructure projects at National Milk Day celebrations in Patna. Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Rajiv Ranjan Singh, also known as Lalan Singh, will be the chief guest. Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, Union Minister of State S P Singh Baghel and Bihar's dairy and fisheries minister Nand Kishore Ram will also be present. The Gopal Ratna Awards, among the country's top honours for the livestock and dairy sector, recognise work to conserve indigenous cattle and buffalo breeds and boost dairy development and productivity. Advertisement They will be given in three categories: dairy farmers rearing indigenous breeds, artificial insemination technicians, and dairy cooperatives or producer organisations. Special awards will go to winners from the northeast and Himalayan states. Projects to be inaugurated include mineral mixture plants in Patna and Muzaffarpur, an effluent treatment plant at Mithila Milk Union in Samastipur, and milk collection and data processing units for dairy cooperatives, all under the National Programme for Dairy Development, an official statement said. The government will also dedicate Namaste India's 2 lakh litre-per-day milk processing plant at Bihta, near Patna, built with support from the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund. Certificates will be handed out for veterinary medicine sales centres under the Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme. On the occasion, the minister will unveil the standard operating procedures and an online portal for rating and grading dairy cooperatives and milk producer organisations, which the government says will improve transparency and performance. The Climate-Resilient Roadmap for India's Livestock and Dairy Sector towards Viksit Bharat @2047 will also be released, alongside the Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2026. The statistics, based on a survey covering March 1, 2025 to February 28, 2026, provide estimates of milk, egg, meat and wool production, state-wise output and per capita availability. Other events include a dialogue with progressive dairy farmers and the launch of Sudha-brand makhana kheer and rabri, along with the handover of keys for Sudha sales outlets. Farmers, milk federations and cooperatives from across the country are expected to take part. National Milk Day marks the birth anniversary of Verghese Kurien, known as the father of India's White Revolution, who helped make the country the world's largest milk producer. national_raw_news.title: NSA Ajit Doval reaffirms commitment to safety & security of Indian Ocean Region at NSA level...
national_raw_news.content: National Security Advisor Ajit Doval today emphasised the shared maritime and civilisational ties among Indian Ocean littoral states, saying the seas must remain a space that connects nations rather than divides them. Addressing the 8th National Security Advisors’ Meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave in Male, Maldives, Mr Doval called for sustained cooperation among countries in the region to ensure maritime security, regional stability and economic prosperity. He said, the littoral states of the Indian Ocean region share a common maritime space and are connected by civilisational heritage shaped over a long period of history. Mr Doval said the formation of the Colombo Security Conclave in November 2020 was guided by a collective vision to ensure the safety, security and stability of the Indian Ocean Region. He added that the grouping had made considerable progress but still had a long journey ahead. The National Security Advisor also underlined India’s commitment to strengthening the regional grouping, linking the Colombo Security Conclave to New Delhi’s neighbourhood-first policy and its broader MAHASAGAR vision. He noted that the Indian Ocean is important not only for the national security and economic prosperity of countries in the region but also for safeguarding the interests and welfare of their people.

national_raw_news.title: SEBI proposes early payout facility for FPOs in commodity derivatives 17 mins ago 11
national_raw_news.content: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has proposed a new framework allowing Early Pay-Out of funds to Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), participating in the agricultural commodity derivatives segment. In a consultation paper issued today, the move aims to ease working capital constraints faced by FPOs, which currently have to wait until contract expiry to receive funds after depositing agricultural produce in accredited warehouses. Under the proposed framework, FPOs that have marked Early Pay-In of goods against a sell transaction can request an early release of up to 80 percent of the sale value. This facility can be availed up to 30 days prior to the expiry of the derivatives contract, subject to specified conditions. To ensure market integrity and systemic stability, SEBI has proposed strict guardrails. Only corporate trading members with a minimum net worth of three crore rupees will be eligible to offer this facility, and their total exposure cannot exceed three times their net worth. Furthermore, once an FPO receives an early pay-out, it will not be permitted to square off that trading position. The proposal aims to reduce delays in receiving payments and help FPOs make timely payments to their member farmers. SEBI has invited public comments on the proposal till 16th December 2026.

national_raw_news.title: Air passenger service inflation surges to 35.52% in Q2 2 hours ago 34
national_raw_news.content: Inflation in air passenger services surged to 35.52 per cent on an annual basis in the second quarter of the current fiscal year, making it the highest among the seven service sectors. According to the Provisional Service Producer Price Indices (SPPIs) data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry today, inflation in the Banking Service Contribution index rose to 3.86 per cent and railway service price index increased to 1.38 per cent during the same period. In contrast, Prices in pension fund management services eased significantly to 1.01 per cent from 5.48 per cent in the preceding quarter. Securities transaction service prices recorded steep deflation of 6.93 per cent. Meanwhile, banking service contribution index moderated to 3.96 per cent in the second quarter. The Provisional Service Producer Price Index measures the average price received by producers in seven major service sectors including banking, securities transactions, insurance, management of pension funds, railways (freight and passenger), air (passenger) transport, and telecom. The government in June came out with the maiden PPI data for both goods and services to better reflect price movement at producer’s level, paving the way for phasing out wholesale price index (WPI)-based inflation numbers in the next five years. Thereafter, in August the services PPI data was issued.

national_raw_news.title: Reasi Police attaches 29 kanals of land belonging to five Pakistan-based terror handlers 5 hours ago 77
national_raw_news.content: Intensifying its crackdown on terror networks and their financial support structures, Reasi Police has attached immovable properties measuring approximately 29 kanals (around 3 acres) belonging to five Pakistan-based terror handlers in Mahore and adjoining areas of the district. Akashvani Jammu Correspondent reports that the action was carried out in connection with an FIR registered at Police Station Mahore under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and E&IMCO Act. The attached properties include 2 kanals and 7 marlas belonging to Mohd Qayoom alias Abdul Qayoom of Shadole, Mahore; 3 kanals and 8 marlas of Bashir Ahmed alias Masoom of Badder, Mahore; 3 kanals and 10 marlas of Shokat Ali of Hunder, Arnas; 15 kanals and 19 marlas of Manzoor Ahmed of Khanti, Thuroo; and 3 kanals and 10 marlas of Imtyaz Ahmed of Thuroo. The attachment proceedings were conducted by a police team led by SDPO Mahore, along with the SHO Mahore and other police personnel, in the presence of the Executive Magistrate, Mahore, and independent witnesses. According to the investigation, the individuals had exfiltrated to Pakistan for terrorist training and are presently operating from across the border as terror handlers, allegedly involved in directing and coordinating terrorist activities in the region. Police investigations also indicated that the properties could be transferred or disposed of, with the proceeds potentially being used to finance terrorist activities. The properties were identified and verified in coordination with the Revenue Department, and the requisite legal formalities were completed after obtaining approval from the Director General of Police, for initiating attachment proceedings under the UAPA. Police further informed that properties belonging to five other Jammu and Kashmir Nationalised Persons (JKNOPs) had also been attached on July 30 as part of the ongoing action against terror-linked networks. The latest action is aimed at dismantling the financial and logistical support system of terrorism by depriving Pakistan-based handlers of assets that could potentially be used to sustain terror activities.

national_raw_news.title: President Droupadi Murmu calls upon youth to draw inspiration from Odisha’s maritime heritage
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has said the younger generation of the country has much to learn from the courage and skills of ancient maritime traders. Addressing Bali Jatra Festival 2026 at Kataka in Odisha, she urged people to draw inspiration from the past to shape the present and build a brighter future. The President said that the Bali Jatra is a unique festival which celebrates the glorious history of Odisha. She said that the merchants from Odisha used to travel to distant lands to engage in trade and commerce. President Murmu said that through trade, they accomplished many significant things for the country. She said, they discovered new maritime routes and strengthened international relations. The President noted that the historical connection between Odisha and Bali can be transformed into modern commercial and cultural cooperation. She also expressed happiness that cultural troupes from Indonesia are participating in this year’s Bali Jatra and that the Odisha Festival is being celebrated in Bali, featuring Odisha’s dance and music, handlooms, handicrafts, and traditional cuisine. The President expressed confidence that such cultural exchanges will strengthen the historical ties between India and Indonesia. She said, India’s stature on the international stage has grown. While there is unrest in many parts of the world and instability in the global economy, India’s economy continues to remain strong. This is a promising indicator of our journey toward becoming Viksit Bharat, she said.

Advertisement India TodayNE Nov 25, 2026 , Updated Nov 25, 2026, 4:02 PM IST Follow us: A book exploring the growth, evolution and challenges of regional cinema in India, titled Bharotor Aancholik Chalacchitra: Uttaan aru Pratyahban, authored by acclaimed film critic and writer Dr. Dipsikha Bhagawati, was formally unveiled at the ongoing 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. The book was launched at the Press Information Bureau (PIB) conference room by Smita Vats Sharma, Director General, West Zone, Press Information Bureau. Smita Saikia, Media and Communication Officer, PIB Assam, and Akashneel Sharma, an officer of the Indian Information Service (IIS), were also present at the event. Dr. Bhagawati, a recipient of the Best Film Critic Award at the 9th Assam State Film Awards, is a film critic, author, translator and academic contributor to Assamese literature and cinema. Her work focuses on film criticism and regional cinema, with contributions appearing in several national and international publications. She is also a commissioned writer for the National Book Trust, India, under the Ministry of Education, and has received the Translation Fellowship of the Publication Board, Government of Assam. She is a British Council-nominated Master Trainer in English Language Teaching and participated in Hong Kong FILMART 2026 as an invitee. Her film reviews and critical writings have been published in platforms including FIPRESCI E-CineIndia, FilmBuff, Journal of Indian Cinema, The Sentinel, The Assam Tribune, Prakash, Satsori and Dainik Asom. Dr. Bhagawati has also served on jury, preview and screening committees at several national and international film festivals. These include the Kautik International Film Festival in Uttarakhand, the New York Indian Film Festival as part of the FCCI Jury, the Guwahati Asian Film Festival (2025–26) and the Waterfront Indie Film Festival in Mumbai. Trained in Film Appreciation at the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, she has authored five books. Her contributions to film scholarship have received international academic recognition, with her books catalogued in the libraries of the Library of Congress, the American Center, Stanford University and the University of Iowa. She has also represented the media as a PIB delegate at IFFI, Goa, on multiple occasions and has participated in and moderated discussions and panel sessions on cinema. The unveiling at IFFI marks another recognition of her contribution to film criticism and scholarship, particularly in the field of regional Indian cinema. national_raw_news.content: Indian Army's Team Mountain Eagles Marks Aviation Milestone With Successful Landing And Refuelling On NH-754K In Gujarat Defence Indian Army's Team Mountain Eagles Marks Aviation Milestone With Successful Landing And Refuelling On NH-754K In Gujarat Swarajya Staff Nov 25, 2026 | Updated 08:56 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Indian Army's aero-adventure team, ‘Team Mountain Eagles’ (Pic Via PIB) The Indian Army's Team Mountain Eagles achieved a historic milestone yesterday when four aircraft successfully landed and refuelled on NH-754K near Patan district in Gujarat. The formation, comprising two microlight aircraft and two powered hang gliders, demonstrated the first-ever landing of such a formation on a national highway or expressway in India. The expedition team from the Army Adventure Nodal Centre at the Military College of Telecommunication Engineering in Mhow, Madhya Pradesh, took off from Kandla Airport and landed on the Amritsar-Jamnagar Expressway near Bakutra Toll Plaza in Santalpur Tehsil. Part of the ongoing "Wings of Valour and Unity" Expedition, the operation showcased the capability of national highways to serve as alternative emergency landing grounds for small aircraft. The demonstration highlighted the strong civil-military cooperation, with the National Highways Authority of India and local civil administration coordinating all arrangements. Officials from NHAI, including a director, along with the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Tehsildar and local police authorities personally supervised the operation. The event marks a significant achievement for Team Mountain Eagles in demonstrating precision flying skills.
